Italy’s Casalgrande Immobiliare Files for Bankruptcy Amid Market Pressures

ROME, June 14 — Casalgrande Immobiliare S.p.A., a prominent real estate company based in Milan, filed for bankruptcy on Friday, citing prolonged financial difficulties and declining demand in Italy’s property market. The move has immediately impacted the company’s ongoing operations, with several major development projects now suspended and uncertainty looming over its property portfolio.

The bankruptcy proceedings were initiated at the Milan Tribunal following what the company described as “unsustainable financial pressures” linked to falling sales and tightening credit conditions. Casalgrande Immobiliare, which focuses on residential and commercial property development, had been one of the region’s most active real estate developers over the past two decades.

“The Board of Directors has taken the difficult decision to seek bankruptcy protection to safeguard the interests of creditors and stakeholders,” the company said in a statement. “We regret the impact this will have on our employees and the communities where we operate.”

Current projects in Rome, Milan and Turin are now on hold while administrators assess the company’s assets and liabilities. According to a source close to the proceedings, around 120 employees have been placed on temporary leave as the company awaits further instructions from the court-appointed administrator.

Industry observers say Casalgrande Immobiliare’s insolvency reflects broader challenges facing Italy’s real estate market, including rising interest rates and sluggish demand for new properties. “The bankruptcy of a company of this size is a sign of the pressures many in the sector are facing,” said Lucia Ferrara, an analyst at the Italian Real Estate Federation. “It will take time to see how this affects ongoing developments and investor confidence within real estate.”

Trade unions representing real estate workers expressed concern about job security and the fate of projects halfway through completion. “Our priority is to protect the rights of employees and ensure transparency throughout the bankruptcy process,” said Giovanni Rinaldi, spokesperson for the National Union of Real Estate Workers.

The Milan Tribunal will now oversee the administration of Casalgrande Immobiliare’s assets, with creditors expected to submit claims in the coming weeks. The company’s statement said it hopes “an orderly process will allow for the best possible outcome for all parties involved,” but acknowledged that the future of its developments remains uncertain.

No timeline has been provided for the resolution of the bankruptcy case, and further updates are expected as administrators begin their review.
